articles.body:
Hello,

This is a compliance matter rather than a bug report, or at least it has become one.

In four cases from the June call our register shows an application received before the closing time, but the enclosures the applicant refers to are not in the case and there is no trace of them anywhere in the audit trail. Two of the applicants have now written to us formally and one has said the word "överklagande".

We are a public authority. If an applicant asserts they filed something before the closing time and our system holds no record either way, we cannot demonstrate that the decision was taken on a complete basis. I need to know what your audit trail records at the moment a document is offered to the system, even if the document itself never lands.

Best regards,
Håkan Nyberg
Programme director, Regionalt Utvecklingsverket
articles.subject: We cannot prove when an applicant filed their enclosures

articles.body:
Dear Håkan,

Thank you for framing it so precisely, it helps.

Today the audit trail records a document when it has been stored. There is no entry for an attempt that did not complete, which is exactly the gap you are describing. I will not defend that design, it is a fair criticism and I am taking it to our engineers.

On the four cases: if you give me the case numbers and approximate times we can look in the request logs, which do keep more than the audit trail does. That may let you establish what happened in those specific cases even though the audit trail is silent.

Kind regards,
Sara Holm
Support lead, Minso
articles.subject: Re: We cannot prove when an applicant filed their enclosures

articles.body:
> if you give me the case numbers and approximate times

Case numbers: RUV-2026-1180, RUV-2026-1194, RUV-2026-1207, RUV-2026-1233. All in the last week before the closing time on 15 June, all late afternoon. The applicants describe sitting with the form for a long time before sending, which I mention in case it matters.

Three of the four concern the same kind of enclosure, the financial annex, which tends to be the heaviest document in the set.

Håkan Nyberg
articles.subject: Re: We cannot prove when an applicant filed their enclosures

articles.body: Request logs show a 401 on the document endpoint for three of the four case numbers, all late afternoon, all after long sessions. Same signature as the other two customers. This one has a legal dimension the others do not, so it should drive the priority.
articles.subject: We cannot prove when an applicant filed their enclosures

articles.body:
Dear Håkan,

We found request log entries for three of the four cases showing a rejected request at the times the applicants describe. I can produce a written extract for those three, which should let you show that something was in fact offered to the system.

For the fourth case we have nothing in the window given.

Separately, we are treating the missing audit trail entry as a defect and not as expected behaviour.

Kind regards,
Sara
